affected_system: fixed-route public transit service and passenger connections
alternatives: screen feasible locations against the largest access gaps for accessible transfer and operational recovery hubs
co-optimize distributed and high-capacity locations for accessible transfer and operational recovery hubs
pair network-constrained hub location with timetable dependencies with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Trips, stops, vehicle observations, disruptions, and calendars share a versioned service day.
Passenger loads and transfer behavior are measured or represented as bounded assumptions.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: retain only existing approved locations for accessible transfer and operational recovery hubs.

constraints.description: The transit reliability and passenger continuity site must respect declared land control, accessibility, permitting, safety, and operating feasibility.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: transit chief operating officer and service-planning director
decision_question: Where should timed-transfer, layover, charging, and passenger-recovery capacity be located?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The transit reliability and passenger continuity site must respect declared land control, accessibility, permitting, safety, and operating feasibility.
independence_key.decision_object: accessible transfer and operational recovery hubs
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for accessible transfer and operational recovery hubs passes documented checks for parcel control, legal authority, environmental review, access, capacity, and operator responsibility.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: network-constrained hub location with timetable dependencies
independence_key.primary_outcome: passengers beyond a reliable accessible transfer

intended_claim: A versioned site design for comparing declared alternatives affecting accessible transfer and operational recovery hubs, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: passengers beyond a reliable accessible transfer
distributional gap in passengers beyond a reliable accessible transfer
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call a candidate hub accessible, permitted, or operationally feasible without verification.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for accessible transfer and operational recovery hubs passes documented checks for parcel control, legal authority, environmental review, access, capacity, and operator responsibility.

title: Site accessible transfer and recovery hubs
transportability_risks: Fare policy, headways, fleet, labor rules, topology, and passenger behavior vary by operator.
Reliability metrics may not transfer between schedule-based and frequency-based service.
